_comment: The one filter grammar all three surfaces parse and highlight from (UI spec §1.1 'filter.grammar.json', the TUI portability rule). Grammar form is canonicalised from the TUI's shipped crates/aitm-tui/src/filter.rs header; atom *names* and meanings follow the approved UI spec (§1.1) + foundation §2.7. filter.conformance.json is the test every surface must pass.

notes: Juxtaposition is AND: `~u login ~m POST` == `~u login & ~m POST`.
Precedence, tightest first: `!`, `&` (explicit or implicit), `|`. `(` `)` override it. `&` and `|` are left-associative.
A bare word (or bare /re/) is `~u word` (see bare_word).

An atom's argument is the next word, quoted string or /regex/ token. `pattern` atoms take any of the three; `literal` atoms refuse a /regex/ (error regex-not-allowed); `none` atoms take no argument, so a following word is a separate AND term.
Text arguments match case-insensitively as substrings, with `*` (any run) and `?` (one char) wildcards. A /…/ argument is a case-insensitive regex unless it says (?-i).
A quoted argument ("…" or '…') may contain spaces and delimiters; there are no escapes inside quotes. A word ends at whitespace or one of ( ) & |.

A /re/ token needs a closing `/` followed by a delimiter or the end; `\` escapes the next character and both are kept in the regex source. Otherwise the text is an ordinary word (so `/api/login` is a word).
Atom aliases are normalised in the AST (`~t` parses to atom `~c`).
Empty or whitespace-only input is 'no filter' (null AST, no error).
Nesting of `!` and `(` is bounded at max_depth; deeper input is refused, not recursed into.

atoms.name: method
atoms.description: HTTP method equals the argument (GET, POST, ...).

atoms.name: status
atoms.description: Response status: an exact code (200) or a class (4xx).

atoms.name: header
atoms.description: A header name or value contains / matches the argument. Needs flow detail (F5).

atoms.name: body
atoms.description: The body contains / matches the argument. Needs flow detail (F5).

atoms.name: query
atoms.description: The query string contains / matches the argument.

atoms.name: agent
atoms.description: The flow was produced by the agent (replay, request.send, poc.run).

atoms.name: scope
atoms.description: The flow's host is in the authorised scope.

atoms.name: websocket
atoms.description: The flow is a WebSocket flow.

atoms.name: paused
atoms.description: The flow is paused at an intercept.

atoms.name: l4
atoms.description: The flow is an L4 (packet) flow. M5-gated.

atoms.name: tcp
atoms.description: An L4 flow whose decoded protocol is TCP. M5-gated.

atoms.name: udp
atoms.description: An L4 flow whose decoded protocol is UDP. M5-gated.

atoms.name: icmp
atoms.description: An L4 flow whose decoded protocol is ICMP. M5-gated.

combinators.name: and
combinators.description: Both sides match. Optional: juxtaposition is also AND.

operators.name: equals
operators.description: The field equals the value exactly.

operators.name: regex
operators.description: The value is a regular expression.

operators.name: jsonpath
operators.description: A JSONPath / jq expression over a body field.

bijection._comment: The GUI stacked-filter model (Field · Operator · Value, rows joined AND/OR) <-> the ~-atom text form, so a GUI's 'advanced view' is exactly the TUI's native expression. The atom set the spec fixes covers only part of foundation §2.7's field list and operator list; the remainder is declared unmapped here (GUI-only, no portable text form yet) rather than invented. Widening the atom set is a spec change.

operator_to_text.equals: pattern atoms: an anchored regex `~u /^exact$/`; literal atoms (~m ~s ~c): the bare argument

bijection.request_response_note: ~h and ~b match either side; the stacked Request/Response split has no distinct atom, so both fields map to the same atom.
